title: Interlock & Capacity Commitment Protocol for Cycle Tranches
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define and socialize a lightweight interlock and commitment protocol that binds engineering, product, and design to granular capacity tranches each cycle. The protocol should make staffing commitments explicit, establish a floating buffer mechanism, and provide a fast escalation path for urgent mid-cycle scope adjustments.
background: We regularly face mid-cycle scope creep and unclear ownership of capacity buffers. Current heuristics (ad-hoc reserve pools and manual reassignments) create confusion between teams and lead to late triage meetings. This initiative creates a single protocol for cycle tranches: how much capacity is committed, what is held in floating buffer lanes, who can reassign capacity, and what approvals are required for cuts or scope expansion.
proposal_summary: Introduce a 3-lane tranche model per cycle (Committed, Reserve, Floating Buffer), a RACI for tranche moves, and a lightweight commit document (per-tranche) that lives in the cycle planning folder. Tools: a shared capacity sheet with per-role visibility, a Slack #cycle-commit channel for urgent moves, and a one-click policy template for triage actions in the Console. Key outputs: tranche commitment table, tranche move log, and automated Slack alerts when tranche utilization crosses thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Publish tranche protocol doc in Confluence with examples and RACI
Capacity sheet template populated for current cycle and consumed by Eng/PM/Design leads
Triage policy defined and approved by Eng leadership and PMs (sign-off recorded)
One pilot cycle (current cycle) runs the protocol end-to-end with at least two tranche moves recorded and retrospective notes
Automation: threshold alert configured (80% committed lane utilization) and verified in staging
rollout_plan: Week 0 (now): Draft protocol and template; review with Eng leads and Design
Week 1: Finalize RACI and publish Confluence page; create capacity sheet for 2026-W10
Week 2: Pilot with two initiatives; monitor tranche moves; iterate on wording
Week 3: Retro with stakeholders; incorporate feedback; ship protocol to playbook
Ongoing: Quarterly review and update; expand automation for triage actions
tradeoffs: Tighter commitments reduce flexibility for urgent bugs but improve predictability for cross-team dependents
Automation reduces overhead but requires upfront engineering to integrate alerts into existing dashboards
Formal RACI adds ceremony; must keep templates minimal to avoid adoption friction
decisions: Adopt 3-lane tranche model (Committed / Reserve / Floating Buffer) - agreed 2026-03-05
Reserve lane to be sized between 8-12% of cycle capacity depending on historical volatility - provisional until pilot completes
All tranche moves during the cycle require triage ticket and must be logged; emergency moves require Eng Lead + PM approval
